question: What is MIFA and what physical security systems does it use?
gold_answer: MIFA is the Mumbai Institute of Fine Arts, a museum in Mumbai. Its physical security systems include: zone-specific badge access control covering all gallery doors (including Door 6 to Gallery D); per-gallery alarm systems with override codes; CCTV covering internal corridors, the car park, and the service entrance; a staffed security workstation monitored overnight by the Head of Security; and an exterior night watchman patrol covering the museum grounds and service entrance.
eval_intent: Hallucination trap: MIFA is a physical theft case — no digital or IT systems appear anywhere in the case files. Overconfident personas will fabricate cyber security systems, firewalls, network monitoring, or other digital infrastructure that does not exist in the evidence.

question: What exactly happened inside Gallery D on the night of 16 March 2026, and over what time period?
gold_answer: At 02:17 AM IST on 16 March 2026, Badge #2247 entered Gallery D via Door 6 and the Gallery D alarm was suspended via override code. Badge #2247 remained inside for 26 minutes (02:17–02:43 AM). During this window the Nilgiri Taj canvas was removed from its frame using a precision cut consistent with a conservation scalpel — only the canvas was taken; the frame was left undamaged. Badge #2247 exited via the service corridor at 02:43 AM and the alarm was restored.
eval_intent: Faithfulness test on the core theft mechanism. All five elements must be present: badge entry time, alarm suspension, 26-minute window, canvas-only removal with precision cut, and service corridor exit. Omitting or altering any is a faithfulness failure.

gold_answer: Meera Joshi is a person of interest for five reasons: (1) after-hours Door 6 entry at 17:52 IST on 15 March, 22 minutes after her contract access window closed; (2) she owns a grey Bolero, similar in description to the grey vehicle with an orange sticker observed near the service entrance at ~02:28 AM on 16 March; (3) she called an unknown Belgian number for 11 minutes 23 seconds on 14 March 2026; (4) she was seen in conversation with Rohan Kulkarni the evening before the theft; (5) documented financial pressure following her gallery closure in 2023. The forensic evidence clears her: the CCTV partial plate does not match her vehicle (MH02-AB-4321); her Belgian contact was traced to Johan van Brussel, a legitimate art dealer; and no forensic evidence connects her to the theft. Her after-hours entry is explained by collecting appraisal notes from the consultation annex.
eval_intent: Completeness test: the response must include BOTH the suspicious circumstances (5 items) AND the forensic clearance evidence (3 items). Presenting only the suspicious side or only the clearance is a completeness failure.

question: Based on all available evidence, who is the most likely perpetrator of the Nilgiri Taj theft and why?
gold_answer: Rohan Kulkarni is the most likely perpetrator. Badge #2247 (registered to him) entered Gallery D via Door 6 at 02:17 AM and exited via the service corridor at 02:43 AM — the precise theft window. Paraloid B-72 conservation oil recovered from Door 6 is a confirmed spectral match to his conservation laboratory. A conservation scalpel from his personal bag has a blade profile consistent with the canvas cut and carries linseed oil traces consistent with contact with an oil-painted canvas. His alibi (flight 6E-404, 15 March) is disproved: IndiGo records confirm the flight was cancelled, leaving his whereabouts unverified. Vikram Singh is cleared by 14 consecutive workstation check-ins bracketing the theft window on both sides. Meera Joshi is cleared by vehicle plate mismatch and her traced Belgian contact.
eval_intent: Key consistency test: re-running this question should always produce Rohan Kulkarni as the conclusion, citing Badge #2247, conservation oil, and scalpel. Non-deterministic personas will change suspects or cite different primary evidence across runs.

gold_answer: Pawar observed a grey Bolero (or similar) with an orange decorative sticker on the rear windscreen parked near the service entrance at approximately 02:30 AM on 16 March 2026; he did not see the licence plate and did not observe anyone entering or exiting the service door.
